name: Arizona

events.title: Statehood
events.text: Arizona became the 48th state on February 14, 1912.

events.title: 1930 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1930 census, Arizona kept 1 seat in the House. It elected its one member statewide (at-large).

events.title: 1940 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1940 census, Arizona's House delegation grew from 1 to 2 seats.

events.title: Statewide (general ticket) elections
events.text: In the 78th through 80th Congresses (1943–1949), Arizona elected all of its representatives statewide on a general ticket instead of by district.

events.title: 1950 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1950 census, Arizona kept 2 seats in the House.

events.title: 1960 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1960 census, Arizona's House delegation grew from 2 to 3 seats.

events.title: 1970 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1970 census, Arizona's House delegation grew from 3 to 4 seats. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1980 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1980 census, Arizona's House delegation grew from 4 to 5 seats. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 1990 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1990 census, Arizona's House delegation grew from 5 to 6 seats. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: Independent commission created
events.text: Arizona voters approved Proposition 106, moving congressional and legislative map drawing to the Arizona Independent Redistricting Commission. Its first congressional map was used from the 2002 election.

events.title: 2000 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2000 census, Arizona's House delegation grew from 6 to 8 seats. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: 2010 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2010 census, Arizona's House delegation grew from 8 to 9 seats. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

events.title: Arizona State Legislature v. Arizona Independent Redistricting Commission
events.text: The Supreme Court held that the Constitution allows a state's voters to give congressional map drawing to an independent commission.

events.title: 2020 census apportionment
events.text: After the 2020 census, Arizona kept 9 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

compactnessNote: Polsby-Popper compactness (4π × area ÷ perimeter²) measured on the projected district shapes. It describes shape only: coastlines, rivers and county lines lower it too, so a low score is not evidence of intent. "Irregular" marks the least compact 5% of district shapes in each census era nationally.

c081.text: Arizona's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1948 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c088.text: New map drawn after the 1960 census, which raised Arizona's seats from 2 to 3. It was first used in the 1962 election.

c090.text: Arizona's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1966 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c092.text: Not a new map: the historical boundary records show only slight differences in 2 districts from the previous Congress, and no statewide redistricting is recorded for this election.

c093.text: New map drawn after the 1970 census, which raised Arizona's seats from 3 to 4. It was first used in the 1972 election.

c098.text: New map drawn after the 1980 census, which raised Arizona's seats from 4 to 5. It was first used in the 1982 election.

c103.text: New map drawn after the 1990 census, which raised Arizona's seats from 5 to 6. It was first used in the 1992 election.

c108.text: New map drawn after the 2000 census, which raised Arizona's seats from 6 to 8. It was first used in the 2002 election.

c113.text: New map drawn after the 2010 census, which raised Arizona's seats from 8 to 9. It was first used in the 2012 election.

c118.text: New map drawn after the 2020 census, which left Arizona with 9 seats. It was first used in the 2022 election.
